newsitem.title: LEBANON: Most leading shares end week stronger in Beirut.
newsitem.headline: Most leading shares end week stronger in Beirut.

text.p: Most leading shares rose on the Beirut Stock Exchange in the week ending on Friday and brokers said Solidere shares were likely to sustain current price levels in the short term.
The LIBX bank index rose 2.96 percent to 190.83. The LISPI general index rose 1.16 percent to 96.29 and the BLOM general index rose 1.5 percent to 1118.21.
Market turnover was 1,664,936 shares from 1,875,813 a week earlier for a value of $21,012,780 against $25,069,895 -- the highest value of trade on the market since its opening in January 1996.
Solidere A rose nearly one percent to $13 from $12.875 while B shares rose 2.91 percent to $13.25 from that level last week.
Bank shares remained strong on the market. Bank of Beirut rose 6.66 percent to an alltime record of $5 from $4.6875 a week earlier.
Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce rose 2.3 percent to $22 from $21.5. The stock hit an alltime high of $22.5 on July 21. Banque Audi was unchanged at $28.625.
Solidere shares which soared last week to their highest levels in two years at $13.75, were fluctuating in profit taking.
"The shares will continue trading between the high $11 and high $13 for sometime," a broker who asked not to be named told Reuters.
"The shares did well this week and the volume was great," another broker added.
Weekly turnover in the shares of Solidere, Lebanon's biggest company, was 1,241,601 shares.
Solidere global depositary receipts traded at $16.5 on Friday from $15.225 a week earlier on the London Stock Exchange.
Of the four listed industrial firms, Ciments Libanais was flat at $1.2813. There was no trade in tilemaker Uniceramic, pipemaker Eternit or Ciments Blancs.
